title: Certificates of Deposit: which penalty, and which withdrawal behind it, is examined for a grace-period reversal
content:
## Scope

When a Certificates of Deposit certificate is examined for a penalty charged on money taken out during its grace period, this rule fixes the penalty entry examined and the withdrawal entry it is traced back to.

## Rule

1. **The penalty.** The penalty examined is the certificate's most recent penalty entry, by posted date. Its amount and its posted date are read from that entry.
2. **The withdrawal behind it.** The withdrawal the penalty belongs to is the withdrawal entry named by the penalty entry's source item reference.
3. **Earlier penalties.** An earlier penalty is examined under this rule only while it is the certificate's most recent penalty. Otherwise it is left to the bank's general penalty reversal rules.

## Tracing chain

Most recent penalty entry → its amount and posted date → its source item reference → the withdrawal entry it names.

## Illustrative case (hypothetical ledger)

| Entry | Posted | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Withdrawal W1 | 4 February | 2000.00 to an official check |
| Penalty P1 | 4 February | 14.20, source item W1 |
| Withdrawal W2 | 21 November | 2750.00 to a savings account |
| Penalty P2 | 21 November | 23.64, source item W2 |

- The penalty examined is P2, the most recent: amount 23.64, posted 21 November.
- The withdrawal behind it is W2, named by P2's source item reference, not W1.
- P1 is not examined under this rule, because it is no longer the most recent penalty.

## Points of judgement

**Is the withdrawal found by looking for one posted on the same day as the penalty?**
No. It is the withdrawal entry named by the penalty entry's source item reference.
